historical_references.context: Khushhaal was a Persian prince who ruled Khorasan (a region in present-day Iran) during the early Abbasid era. He is famous for his valour and generosity, and was a patron of scholars and poets. He was a contemporary of Harun al-Rashid and Caliph Ma'mon, and his death is believed to have occurred around 820 CE.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Aghanis Al-Siqah Al-Nafisah, Volume 1, page 210 The name Khushhaal carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Khushhaal was also mentioned in the epic poem Aghanis by Ferdowsi, as the brave and just ruler of the city of Balkh (present-day Afghanistan). He is described as a model of chivalry and loyalty, who was loved by his people and respected by his enemies.
